chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that an angel from the angels of Allah, who had a great status with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, was reproached, so he was lowered from the sky to the earth. So he went to Idris (peace be upon him) and said: 'You have a status from Allah, so intercede for me with your Lord.'

So he prayed for three nights without ceasing, and fasted during its days without breaking the fast. Then he supplicated to Allah, the Exalted, during the pre-dawn hours regarding the angel. The angel said: 'You have been granted your request, and my wings have been released for me, and I wish to recompense you, so ask me for a need.'

He said: 'Show me the Angel of Death, perhaps I find comfort in him, for nothing seems pleasing to me along with his mention.' So he spread his wing, then said: 'Ride!' So he ascended with him, seeking the Angel of Death in the lowest heaven.

It was said to him: 'Ascend.' So he encountered him between the fourth and fifth heavens. The angel said: 'O Angel of Death, why do I see you frowning?' He said: 'Strange is the matter. I am beneath the shade of the Throne, where I was commanded to capture the soul of a human being between the fourth and fifth heavens.'

So Idris (peace be upon him) heard, bit his knuckle in astonishment, and fell from the wing of the angel. His soul was captured at that spot, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And We elevated him to a high place.'
ai.seo_question: What happened to the Angel of Death when he sought intercession from Prophet Idris?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Idris (peace be upon him) intercedes for a fallen angel, earning the release of his wings and the opportunity to request a favor. His choice to see the Angel of Death to find comfort in his presence leads to his immediate death upon hearing the angel's purpose, fulfilling the Quranic promise of elevation. This event highlights the Shia understanding of *Raf'* (elevation) not merely as physical ascension but as a spiritual station achieved through divine decree and proximity to death.
